intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that atrial standstill-1 (ATRST1) is caused by mutation in the SCN5A gene. Coinheritance of rare polymorphisms in the gene encoding the atrial-specific gap junction protein connexin-40 (Cx40) may modify whether the disorder appears.

paragraphs.text: Atrial standstill is a rare arrhythmia that occasionally appears to be genetically determined (Groenewegen et al., 2003). The surface ECG shows no P waves, and the atrium cannot be captured by pacing (Makita et al., 2005). Familial atrial standstill has been reported together with atrioventricular block (Williams et al., 1972) and with syncope, dilated cardiomyopathy, and sudden cardiac death (Fazelifar et al., 2005).

paragraphs.text: Groenewegen et al. (2003) screened candidate genes in a large family with atrial standstill. They found a novel mutation in the SCN5A gene, asp1275-to-asn (D1275N), in all 3 affected living relatives and in 5 unaffected relatives. The affected deceased relative was an obligate carrier. They also found 2 closely linked polymorphisms in regulatory regions of the gene for the atrial-specific gap junction protein connexin-40 (Cx40), at nucleotides -44 (G-A) and +71 (A-G). Eight relatives were homozygous for both polymorphisms, a genotype found in only about 7% of control subjects, and 3 of these 8 were affected. The 3 living patients were the only relatives who had inherited both the rare Cx40 genotype and the D1275N mutation. Compared with wildtype channels, D1275N channels showed a small depolarizing shift in activation. In reporter gene analysis, the rare Cx40 genotype reduced reporter gene expression compared with the more common genotype. Groenewegen et al. (2003) proposed that each genetic change has a relatively benign functional effect, but that together they eventually lead to total atrial standstill.

paragraphs.text: Makita et al. (2005) screened SCN5A and atrial-specific genes, including Cx40, in the family of an 11-year-old boy with atrial standstill. They found a novel SCN5A mutation, leu212-to-pro (L212P), in the proband and in his father, who was in normal sinus rhythm. In whole-cell patch clamp studies in a heterologous expression system, the L212P channel showed a large hyperpolarizing shift in the voltage dependence of both activation (wildtype, -48.1 +/- 0.9 mV; L212P, -63.5 +/- 1.5 mV; P less than 0.001) and inactivation (wildtype, -86.6 +/- 0.9 mV; L212P, -95.6 +/- 0.8 mV; P less than 0.001). Recovery from inactivation was also delayed. The authors then looked for genetic variants that might lessen the effect of L212P. The proband, but not his father, carried Cx40 polymorphisms inherited from his asymptomatic mother. Makita et al. (2005) concluded that SCN5A defects most likely underlie atrial standstill and that coinheritance of Cx40 polymorphisms may modify how the disorder is expressed.
